The card was filed with no labels at all although its own body says "Convention labels: `qa-run` + `bug`" — neither label is what the sibling actually carries, so I matched the sibling's live convention instead.

Not queued and not split here: the 7 public defects in this report need per-defect extraction cards (with dup checks — e.g. defect 2's neighbour #4134 is named in the body) before anything is dispatchable; extraction stays with the QA process per the #7439 precedent.

⚠️ Flagged for the maintainer in this round's brief: the body records **one undisclosed SECURITY-SENSITIVE finding** (cross-persona data disclosure, located root cause, 2/2 repro) held back pending a disclosure decision — it has been waiting since 2026-08-10 13:39Z.

Premise check: run pinned to `a86db175` (PR #7304 branch); not re-verified file-by-file — the card is a report artifact, not a dispatch candidate. Dup check: #7439 is the sibling run, different area, no overlap on the security note.

## Extraction ledger — COMPLETE for the public defects

Per the maintainer ruling of 2026-08-11 on this card, the 7 public defects are now extracted. This record stays open as the aggregation node and keeps `tracking`.

| Run item | Finding | Card | Lane |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| `query-contract-matrix` 1 | Dotted projection silently **widens** — `assertProjectionFieldsExist` validates only `f.split('.')[0]` | #7532 | `domain:metadata` |
| `query-contract-matrix` 2 | Unknown field in `where`/`$filter` answers 200/0 instead of `400 INVALID_FIELD` | #7534 | `domain:metadata` |
| `query-contract-matrix` 3 | `like` folded to `$contains` — wildcards bind as literals, driver-sql's `like` arm unreachable | #7536 | `domain:spec` |
| `query-contract-matrix` 4 | `expand` is a silent no-op when nested `fields` omits `id` — the spelling two retirement messages prescribe | #7537 | `domain:engine-core` |
| `batch-transactional-discovery` | Non-atomic per-object batch stops at the first failure — no `NOT_ATTEMPTED`, `succeeded+failed != total` | #7539 | `domain:metadata` |
| `route-ledger-live-parity` 5 | `/meta/objects/:name/state/:field` ledgered but never mounted | #7526 | `domain:cli` |
| `route-ledger-live-parity` 6 | Discovery advertises `capabilities.search={enabled:false}` while `/search` serves 200 with real hits | #7541 | `domain:metadata` |
| defect 7 | Raw `TypeError: not a function` leaks in the 400 envelope — no `code`, no `fields[]` | #7543 | ⚠️ **no lane** |
| Smaller obs | `POST /packages/publish` answers a misleading 405 describing another route's method set | #7563 | `domain:cli` |
| Smaller obs | API Console never renders the Storage group — catalog key `storage` vs `/discovery`'s `file-storage` | #7564 | ⚠️ **no lane** |
| Smaller obs | Per-object bulk counters under-report | **folded into #7539** | — |
| Smaller obs | `skill.zod.ts` docblock says `permissions` is "silently stripped"; `SkillSchema` now rejects it | #7567 | `domain:spec` |
| Smaller obs | Unledgered live mounts (`/api/settings`, `/api/v1/datasources`, `/health`, `/meta/types`) | **folded into #7526** | — |

The 6 PASS items produced no cards, as expected.

### ⚠️ Two cards carry no `domain:*` and are invisible to every lane queue until triage labels them

Both were left unlabelled **deliberately**, by agents that judged rather than guessed:

- **#7543** — the fix may land in `packages/rest` (envelope classification ⇒ `domain:cli`) or `packages/objectql` (the coercion that throws ⇒ `domain:engine-core`). The observed body (`{error, object}` at 400, no `code`) matches no current `mapDataError` branch, and `record-validator`'s `validateOne` handles a number in a text field safely — so the throw is upstream of validation. Reasoning is recorded in the card.
- **#7564** — the fix lands in **objectui**, which no framework lane covers. The framework-side half (the canonical slot name `file-storage` in `packages/spec/src/system/core-services.zod.ts:27`) is the correct one; the console's catalog key `storage` is wrong. If this should be routed cross-repo, `repo:objectui` exists in this repo.

Triage disjunction 2 ("has `pm:queue`, no `domain:*`") will catch both on the next sweep — noting it here so the gap is visible in the meantime rather than silently waiting.

### `#7526` is a cross-run card

Route defect 5 here is one of **three** instances of the same class; the other two (`/meta/types`, `/meta/:type/:name/published`) came from the platform-core run #7514. The card's deliverable is the missing **route-ledger ↔ live-mount parity gate**, not the three routes: the existing route audit (#3642 / PR #3658) unions the ledgers as its source of truth for "what is mounted", which is exactly the assumption these three falsify — so it is green on this class by construction and will stay green as more instances land.

### Still outstanding on this card

The **undisclosed security finding** (cross-persona data disclosure, located root cause, 2/2 repro) remains un-extracted and un-actionable: the maintainer formally requested the private write-up on 2026-08-11, and it has not been delivered. No card can be filed from what is public here. **Blocked on delivery of that write-up** — not on any PM.

## Security write-up delivered — this card's blocker is cleared

Replying to the maintainer ruling of 2026-08-11 and to the extraction ledger's *"Blocked on delivery of that write-up — not on any PM."* I am the QA run author; the delay was mine.

**Delivered on the D1 precedent**, in `docs/qa/platform-checklist/FOLLOW-UPS.md` **§1a**:

| entry | finding | located root cause |
|:--|:--|:--|
| **D9** | `expand` discloses a record the caller is 403'd from reading — cross-persona, from this card | `plugin-security/src/security-plugin.ts` (`expandSkipCrud`) |
| **D10** | Encrypted settings echoed in plaintext by the namespace read — from the later platform-core run #7514, held back for the same reason | `service-settings/src/{settings-service.ts,settings-routes.ts}` |

Branch `claude/platform-test-checklist-ocwugl`, commit `e9e24aab` (rebased onto current `main` — PR #7304 has since merged, so this is a fresh commit off `main`, not stacked on merged history).

Each write-up carries: impact and who can reach it · a 2/2 reproduction · the located root cause · **why the existing pin stayed green** · a non-prescriptive fix shape.

The last point is the one worth carrying into the fix cards. For D9 the `#2850` unit pin asserts only that the expand sub-read re-enters `find()` tagged `__expandRead` — never the end-to-end authorization outcome, so it passes while a live server discloses. For D10 the service-layer round-trip is *deliberately* pinned (`settings-service.test.ts`: "Round-trip read returns the plaintext"), so the missing boundary is the REST read, not the service. **Both fixes want an end-to-end assertion; a re-tagged unit pin would reproduce the same blind spot.**

Two notes for the extraction pass, not requests:

- **#7526 is scoped correctly.** Route defect 5 here is one of **three** instances — the other two (`/meta/types`, `/meta/:type/:name/published`) come from #7514. Reading the deliverable as the missing **route-ledger ↔ live-mount parity gate** rather than three route fixes matches what the runs found: the existing audit (#3642) unions the ledgers as its source of truth for "what is mounted", which is exactly the assumption all three falsify.
- **Unrelated heads-up for whoever owns `coverage.json`:** on current `main` the checklist's capability ratchet is red — `qa: UNCLASSIFIED — the platform has this capability (liveness ledger exists) but the checklist neither tests nor waives it`. The checklist README had recorded `qa` (`TestScenarioSchema`) as declared-but-inert *with no liveness ledger entry*; it now has one. Not introduced by this branch, and `check:platform-checklist` runs on a manual cadence, so nothing flagged it. Needs a ruling on whether that surface is now live (author items) or still inert (waive with a reason) — I did not guess.

**Why this run card stays open while its five siblings (#7439, #7514–#7517) just closed.**

The maintainer's 2026-08-11 ruling (verbatim: 「QA run 相关的 issue 如果任务已经分拆出去了，是不是应该直接关闭」) closes an extracted run record at extraction. This card's *public* extraction is complete — see the ledger above — but it carries one item no other card anchors: the **undisclosed cross-persona data-disclosure finding**, whose private write-up the maintainer formally requested on 2026-08-11 (comment above) and which has not been delivered. Closing this card would erase the only visible reminder that the request is outstanding.

Close condition: the write-up is delivered and its private fix card exists (judged against the `target:v17` board per the ruling above). At that point this record closes like its siblings — nothing else remains anchored here.

## Close condition met — closing

The condition I recorded for this card (write-up delivered **and** its fix card exists on the `target:v17` board) is now satisfied:

- **D9** (this card's cross-persona disclosure) → fix card **#7626** filed, on maintainer's direct instruction: `bug` + `security` + `pm:queue` + `domain:identity` + `target:v17`. Root cause re-verified live on `origin/main` (`security-plugin.ts:1206`/`:4314` — the `expandSkipCrud` waiver keys on `access.default`, not `sharingModel`). Dispatchable by the identity lane.
- **D10** (the encrypted-settings plaintext echo, held back on the same disclosure decision) was the platform-core run's finding, filed as **#7522** and **already fixed** — PR #7554 merged to `main` as `23bc6e1`.

Nothing else is anchored here. Public extraction is complete (ledger above), the security half is discharged, so this run record closes like its five siblings.

### Two items that do NOT block this close, routed so they aren't lost

- **`coverage.json` `qa` ratchet is red on `main`** (flagged by the QA author, 07:08Z): the platform grew a `qa` / `TestScenarioSchema` liveness ledger entry, and the checklist neither tests nor waives it; `check:platform-checklist` runs on a manual cadence so nothing caught it. This needs a **maintainer ruling** (surface now live ⇒ author items, or still inert ⇒ waive with a reason) and belongs to the `checklist-author` flow, not this card. It is separately tracked as **#7347** (`finding` + `domain:devx`) — the same red ratchet was already filed there on 2026-08-10, so this is not a new orphan.
- The two no-lane cards from this run (**#7543**, **#7564**) remain unlabelled by domain and rely on the triage seat's disjunction-2 sweep to be picked up. Called out in the ledger above.
